title: A video that changed on disk shows its new frames everywhere the moment it is opened again
goal: If a video file is replaced or re-exported on disk and then opened in Photonz again, scrubbing backwards shows frames from the OLD file until you press play. Whenever a file has changed since Photonz last read it, every picture of it, scrubbing, playing, thumbnails, the filmstrip and its length and size, must come from the new file.
notes:
User, 2026-11-24: "major bug - if I load a video that has been updated on disk, scrubbing backwards seems to show the old video frames until i play". Not reproduced by me.

Likely cause (read in code): Sources/Photonz/MovieFrames.swift MovieLibrary.movie(at:as:) (~46-73) returns the cached MovieRef for a URL it has seen before (refsByURL keyed by the standardized URL alone, 'the same file asked for twice is the same reference, so re-opening a recording re-uses whatever frames of it are already decoded'), with no check that the file is still the same. Everything downstream keys by that MovieRef id: MovieDecoder's AVAssetImageGenerator lanes (generators keyed by movie id, ~176-240, built on the OLD AVURLAsset, which can keep reading the old file's data), keyFrameTables and glimpseGenerators (~246-256), and any frame and filmstrip caches keyed by movie id. Playing likely builds a fresh reader on the URL, which is why play shows the new file. The length and size in the ref are stale too.

Fix direction: identify a file by path plus a fingerprint (file resource identifier / inode, size and content modification date) and treat a changed fingerprint as a new movie: a new MovieRef (or the same id with every per-movie cache forgotten via MovieDecoder.forget and the frame and filmstrip caches dropped), re-read duration, size, sound and pointer track. Check CaptureThumbnail and the History store for path-keyed thumbnails too. Trap: documents hold MovieRef ids; if the ref id changes, an open document's clips must be re-pointed or the old id kept and its caches flushed instead. Sits with the video-perf tasks at the head of the queue at the user's word ('major bug').
acceptance: Reproduced first in the probe at Next defaults: open a recording, scrub and play it, close its window, overwrite the file on disk with a different video (same name; once by writing over it in place and once by replacing it with a new file, as an export or a re-record does), open it again, and scrub backwards and forwards before playing. Record which views show old frames (scrub picture, filmstrip, History thumbnail, poster), and whether the length and picture size are the old ones.

Also the case where the window stays open while the file changes underneath it: say in the audit what happens today and what should (the recommended behaviour is to notice the change and reload the recording, keeping the playhead where it was when it still fits).

After the fix, reopening a changed file never shows a single old frame anywhere, and its length, size, sound and pointer track are read from the new file. A file that has not changed still reuses what was already decoded (no extra decode cost for the common case, measured).

A test that fails on today's code: a unit or integration test that opens a movie, swaps the file at the same path for a different one, opens it again and checks the frame decoded at a scrub time is from the new file. Plus a walk.

Audit under queue/audits/ with before and after pictures. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
